concepts.def: Mass of the substance, in kilograms (kg)

walkthroughs.body_html:
E = m × c × Δθ

Energy (J) = mass (kg) × specific heat capacity (J/kg°C) × temperature change (°C).

Δθ is the Greek letter delta-theta — it just means "change in temperature".

Heat 2 kg of water by 10 °C. SHC of water = 4200 J/kg°C.

E = 2 × 4200 × 10 = 84 000 J.

That's 84 kJ — quite a lot, because water's c is huge.

To find c: c = E ÷ (m × Δθ).

To find Δθ: Δθ = E ÷ (m × c).

Tip: always write the units down with each number — it stops silly mistakes.
